explain.say: An air purifier is a fan in a box of filters. The fan pulls room air in and pushes it through several layers before blowing it back out.

faq.a: HEPA stands for high-efficiency particulate air. It is a pleated mat of tangled glass or plastic fibres that traps at least 99.97 percent of particles 0.3 microns across.
asks: How does a HEPA filter work?

faq.a: It catches large particles like hair, lint and fluff, so they do not clog the expensive fine filter. Many pre-filters can be washed or vacuumed.
asks: Why does my air purifier have two filters?

faq.q: Does an air purifier remove smells?
faq.a: Only if it has an activated carbon filter. The carbon soaks up odour and gas molecules; a HEPA filter alone catches particles but not smells.
asks: Can an air purifier remove cooking smells?

faq.q: How can a filter catch particles smaller than its gaps?
faq.a: Tiny particles do not travel straight. They bump into fibres as air winds through the mat, or jiggle randomly until they touch a fibre and stick.
asks: How can a HEPA filter trap viruses?

faq.q: How big a room can an air purifier clean?
faq.a: It depends on how much air the fan moves. A purifier should be able to filter all the air in the room several times an hour to make a real difference.
asks: What size air purifier do I need?

facts: A true HEPA filter traps at least 99.97 percent of particles 0.3 microns across.
HEPA filters remove particles but not gases; activated carbon is used for smells.
